sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body chestnut brown above; postclypeus distinctly paler; pleurites and legs ochraceous yellowish brown; wings dark smoky. Compound eyes and ocelli rather large for the genus; compound eyes projecting, the ocellus separated from the hyaline margin of the compound eye by about half its short diameter. Postclypeus slightly less than half as long as wide. Number of antennal segments damaged in the OCR of the original (reads "Ik") and not supplied by conjecture; segment 3 very short and narrow, always the shortest of all segments; segment 4 distinctly longer and wider than segment 3; segment 5 about as long as segment 2; subsequent segments very slightly progressively longer. Anterior margin of the pronotum nearly straight and slightly upturned, the sides curving to a fairly broadly rounded, slightly wavy posterior margin; posterior margin of the mesonotum broad, broadly and shallowly concave; posterior margin of the metanotum usually rounded, sometimes slightly concave in the middle. Measurements (mm): body length with wings 9.25—9.50; body length without wings 5.25—5.50; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.00—1.10; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.58 (upper limit damaged); head width 0.85—0.92; greatest diameter of compound eye 0.29; ocellus length 0.10; pronotum length 0.40—0.44; pronotum width 0.64—0.69; forewing length 8.25; forewing width 2.10.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: One of the largest species of the genus. Head hazel brown, darkest anteriorly; labrum orange reddish brown; thorax and legs milky yellowish brown. Head (Fig. 331) with the sides nearly parallel, slightly truncate posteriorly, the anterior dorsal margin with 1 median and 2 lateral very indistinct projections. Labrum slightly longer than wide at its base, evenly narrowing from the base to a rather pointed apex. Mandibles very long, as long as the head capsule, the outer side of the base slightly concave, then widening and extending almost straight to the apex, the apex fairly abruptly incurved, the inner margin distinctly and irregularly serrate. Antennae 13-segmented, reaching the apex of the mandibles; segment 3 always the shortest and narrowest of all segments; segment 4 slightly longer than segment 2. Measurements (mm): body length 5.50—6.40; head length with mandibles 2.73—3.19; head length (to clypeal suture) 1.54—1.70; head width 0.91—0.99; pronotum length 0.36—0.40; pronotum width 0.66—0.71.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The original also records queen measurements: body length 21.00 mm, abdomen width 4.00 mm.

note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), originally in English. The original combination is Miorocerotermes boreus Hill, 1927 (the genus name OCR'd mostly as Miorocerotermes/Microcerotennes). Measurements in mm. OCR problems: in "Antennae of Ik segments" the number of segments in "Ik" is damaged and not supplied by conjecture; in "head, to clypeofrontal suture, long 0.58 - O.o2" the upper limit is damaged and only the readable 0.58 is retained; in "pronotum, long 0.4© - 0.44" the "©" is a misreading of 0, read as 0.40. Distribution: Melville Island, Northern Territory (type locality), Darwin; the original records that the nest of this species is a small rounded lump about 11 × 9 inches, mostly built on dead stumps or surface roots, about half of it underground. The Victorian specimens referred to this species in 1927 have been transferred to M. cavus.
